source.title: Kernel and Rich Regimes in Overparametrized Models
source.authors: Blake E. Woodworth; Suriya Gunasekar; J. Lee; E. Moroshko; P. Savarese; Itay Golan; Daniel Soudry; N. Srebro

record.tranche_reason: The study examines initialization scale, kernel-versus-rich behavior, and final generalization, but it does not measure delayed generalization or the grokking behavior in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The MNIST and CIFAR10 experiments report final test error by initialization scale, alongside training accuracy. They do not report when generalization begins relative to training accuracy saturation. Those final-error findings are recorded under fits_no_version; the kernel-predictor comparisons are references for those findings, not separate results about delayed generalization.
record.test_reason: The paper predates grokking and measures final generalization as a function of initialization scale (kernel vs rich regimes). It never reports when test performance improves relative to training-accuracy saturation on any dataset, so it cannot bear on delayed generalization. Its lazy-to-rich framework is background for V3, but no result tests V3's claim that grokking-like delays can be switched on or off.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. Initialization scale controls the kernel-to-rich transition and generalization: small scale gives rich biases (ℓ1/nuclear-norm-like) and large scale gives kernel (ℓ2) behavior. Depth sharpens the transition and width affects entry into the kernel regime. Standard He initialization (α≈1) sits just at the edge of the kernel regime.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes initialization-scale effects on kernel and rich regimes; it does not apply the grokking recipe or measure delayed generalization.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization scale changes final test error and kernel-versus-rich behavior in the reported experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: On MNIST, final test error is about 1.4% for α≤2 and about 2.4% for α≥50, with all networks at 100% training accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Smaller initialization scale (rich regime) yields better final generalization than large-scale (kernel) initialization at equal training fit.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR10 with a VGG11-like network, final test error depends on α (figure only), while full-network training reaches 100% training accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization scale controls final generalization in deep CNNs via the kernel-to-rich transition.

record.problems: The image experiments report final errors rather than training-time trajectories, so they cannot establish whether test generalization is delayed after training accuracy saturates. CIFAR10 error values are shown in figures without numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant outcomes were omitted. Other experiments (synthetic regression, matrix factorization, and univariate spline behavior) do not report grokking-like delayed generalization.

untested.parts: No algorithmic datasets and no train/test accuracy trajectories.
No circuit formation or progress measures.
Initialization scale is varied on MNIST and CIFAR10, but only final test error and kernel-distance are reported. No delayed generalization after training saturation is measured.
No weight decay, critical dataset size or ungrokking.
No comparison of algorithms learned across runs.
No optimizer or numerical artifact analysis.

missing.what: CIFAR10 test-error-versus-epoch curves for α from 0.75 to 2.0. Smaller α gives slower test-error decrease, which the authors frame as optimization difficulty. No train-accuracy timing is given, so the curves cannot show a delay after saturation; worth noting for V3 comparisons.
Last-layer-only training reference results: 2.7% MNIST test error, and 50.38% CIFAR10 train accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: This is a pre-grokking theory paper, relevant only as background for V3's lazy/rich framing. It has no delayed-generalization measurements. Figure 8's epoch curves are the only trajectories, and they lack train-accuracy timing.

versions.untested_parts: No small algorithmic dataset results or training/test accuracy trajectories after overfitting.
No gradual formation or removal of circuits, Fourier algorithm, or progress measures anticipating a test-accuracy jump.

The study varies initialization scale and reports final generalization on MNIST and CIFAR10, but does not test grokking-like delays, their onset, or whether weight norm switches such delays on or off.
No test of weight decay as an efficiency account, critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
No comparison of algorithms learned across runs.
No test of optimizer or numerical artifacts causing grokking-like delays.

rows.subject: fully-connected depth-2, 5000 hidden unit ReLU network

rows.note: The text reports this final test error range and says every network reached 100% training accuracy; it does not give timing of the test-error change.
rows.check: This is a final test error at α≤2 with no timing information, so it cannot show a grokking-like delay. The 'observed' state is not meaningful against any version.
